deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page reduces meridian zenith distances of alpha Lyrae (Vega) observed at Goettingen from 27 Oct to 26 Dec 1818. The next page does the same for gamma Draconis, using a column of small date-dependent corrections. This is routine positional astronomy, almost certainly toward the latitude of the new observatory and/or the instrument's zenith point. The quantities near 13 deg 2' and near 12 deg 46' are the apparent zenith distance read in two different instrument settings (circle positions). Their half-sum is about 12 deg 54' 33". That agrees with phi - delta for Vega at Goettingen in 1818: about 51 deg 31.8' - 38 deg 37' = 12 deg 55'. That interpretation is mine; the page does not form the half-sum.

TABLE 1 (reduction for the date-dependent correction). For each date the raw reading z_obs is given. A correction c(t) is added; it falls smoothly from +8.53" (27 Oct) to -5.07" (24 Dec), consistent with aberration plus nutation reduction to a fixed mean epoch. Gauss forms z1 = z_obs + c.
- Group A (setting ~13 deg 2'), 27 Oct to 10 Nov: 58.88+8.53=67.41 -> 13 deg 2' 7.41"; 58.68+7.58=66.26; 60.85+7.22=68.07; 59.92+7.05=66.97; 60.08+6.33=66.41. Mean = 35.12/5 = 7.024 -> 13 deg 2' 7.02".
- Group B (setting ~12 deg 46'), 11 Nov to 5 Dec: 28.52+6.16=34.68; 27.73+5.98=33.71; 24.23+5.80=30.03; 29.92+1.59=31.51; 34.58+1.08=35.66; 31.22+0.80=32.02; 33.11+0.52=33.63. The bracketed mean 12 deg 46' 32.54" was written while the December values were still unrevised (see errors).
- Dec 24 (setting A again): 13 deg 2' 9.81" - 5.07 = 13 deg 2' 4.74".
- The entry 'Refraction 1,1201' is log10 of the mean refraction at this zenith distance, i.e. 10^1.1201 = 13.18".

TABLE 2 (refraction). The columns are:
- barometer in Paris inches and lines (27" 11.3''' etc.);
- attached (mercury) thermometer, degrees Reaumur;
- external air thermometer, degrees Reaumur;
- barometric correction to the log of refraction, units 1e-5;
- thermometric correction to the log of refraction, units 1e-5;
- log R = 1.1201 + (b + t)*1e-5;
- R = 10^logR in arcseconds;
- z = z1 + R.
Every row checks: e.g. 27 Oct, 1.1201 + 0.00690 = 1.1270, 10^1.1270 = 13.40", and 7.41 + 13.40 = 20.81.

Scale of the corrections (my inference):
- Barometric term: about 130 units per Paris line, i.e. d log10 p. The zero falls near 27" 9.4''' = 333.4 lines, with a small attached-thermometer effect.
- Thermometric term: about 208 units per degree Reaumur, matching the air-expansion coefficient 0.0047 per degree Reaumur. The zero falls near +7.4 degrees Reaumur.

Refraction-corrected results:
- Group A: 20.81, 19.32, 21.07, 19.98, 19.93; mean 101.11/5 = 20.222 -> 13 deg 2' 20.22".
- Group B: 48.36, 47.34, 43.51, 45.05, 49.13, 45.59, 47.17; mean 326.15/7 = 46.593 -> 12 deg 46' 46.59". The earlier crossed-out means (46.97, 46.91) were superseded.
- Dec 24: 4.74 + 13.90 = 13 deg 2' 18.64". Then 13 deg 2' 19.96" = (5*20.222 + 18.64)/6, the mean of all six setting-A observations (my identification).

OTHER NOTES.
- The bottom list (Dec 24, 25, 26: 13 deg 2' 9.81, 6.78, 7.05) gives raw readings for the following nights. These are not yet reduced, apart from the 6.78 squeezed in at row 24 above.
- Implicit next step (mine, not on page): z_true = (19.96" + 46.59" combined as half-sum) = (13 deg 2' 19.96" + 12 deg 46' 46.59")/2 = 12 deg 54' 33.27". The half-difference, 7' 46.69", is the zenith-point/index error of the setting.
errors: Nov 3 barometric correction: the transcription's -199 does not reproduce log R = 1.1160. Only -299 does: 1.1201 - 0.00412 = 1.11598. -299 also fits the barometer scale (27" 7.1''' lies 2.3 lines below the 333.4-line zero, times ~130 = -299). So the figure is -299, a misreading rather than Gauss's slip.

Dec 4 thermometric correction: +1363 gives log R = 1.1307, but Gauss's 1.1327 (R = 13.57") requires +1563. +1563 also fits the temperature trend (0.1 deg -> 1521, -0.5 deg -> 1648, so -0.1 deg -> ~1563). The entry is +1563.
Dec 4 final value is 32.02 + 13.57 = 45.59, not 47.59. Only 45.59 makes the 7-value mean equal 46.59 as written.

Group B mean 12 deg 46' 32.54" (Table 1) does not match the revised values. The mean of the first three is 32.81; of the first four, 32.48; of all seven, 33.03. The Dec 1, 3, 4 readings are visibly overwritten. 32.54 is presumably the mean of Nov 11-13 + Dec 1 computed before Dec 1 was revised (it would need Dec 1 = 31.74). It is a stale intermediate, not used later; the refraction-corrected mean 46.59 is computed correctly from the revised values.
Oct 27 raw reading: the image shows 58.88 (overwritten), not 58.68. 58.88 + 8.53 = 67.41 = 2' 7.41" confirms it.
All other additions, logarithms, antilogarithms and means check to the last digit.

results.what: Reduction of observed zenith distances by a date-dependent correction (aberration/nutation reduction to mean place), then averaging per instrument setting
results.modern_name: Reduction to mean place (annual aberration + nutation); combination of observations in two circle positions to eliminate index error

results.what: Refraction computed as log R = log R_mean + barometric term + thermometric term, using Paris-inch barometer and Reaumur thermometers; R_mean = 13.18" at z ~ 12 deg 55'
results.modern_name: Atmospheric refraction reduction with pressure/temperature factors (Bradley/Mayer/Bessel-type tables)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley, Tobias Mayer, Laplace; tabulated by Bessel (Fundamenta Astronomiae, 1818)

results.what: Weighted combination: 13 deg 2' 19.96" as the mean of 5 + 1 observations; implicit half-sum of two settings giving z ~ 12 deg 54' 33" for Vega (toward the Goettingen latitude)
results.modern_name: Arithmetic mean / elimination of zenith-point error; latitude from meridian zenith distance

deep.surprise_reason: These are purely routine observational reductions (aberration correction, refraction from barometer and thermometer, means) of Vega zenith distances, as Gauss did for the Goettingen latitude around 1818. There is no mathematical novelty; the only interest is archival (which instrument, which refraction constants).

checkable.asserts: Mean of the 7 revised group-B values = 33.034, not the written 32.54
Half-sum of the two settings = 12 deg 54' 33.27" (33.275 s beyond 12 deg 54'), close to phi - delta for Vega at Goettingen 1818
Barometer 27" 11.3''' vs 27" 4.1''' differ by ~943 units of 1e-5 in log, matching +252 - (-696) = 948

transcription_corrections: Title: the manuscript has 'alpha Leyer' (Gauss's spelling of Lyra); 'alpha Lyrae' is the intended star.
Group B bracket in the refraction table: the crossed-out means are 46.97 and 46.91, and the final value is 12 deg 46' 46.59".
'27 deg 11'3' in the first column of table 2 is a barometer reading, 27 Paris inches 11.3 lines, not degrees; subsequent entries are lines (7.1, 4.1, ...).
'Refraction 1,1201' is log10 of the mean refraction (13.18"), the base value to which the corrections are added.
